metadata.title: Transitional thermal creep of sealed concrete (Fahmi et al. 1972), OOFEM-native calibration of Havlasek & Jirasek (2012)
metadata.validation_method: Creep-test simulation vs digitized experimental curve
metadata.validation_target: Fig.5 (re-digitised): -0.407e-3 at 37 d (end of the 23 degC phase), -0.845e-3 at 70 d, -1.287e-3 at 145 d, peak -1.312e-3, unloading at 154.7 d dropping to ~ -1.08e-3. Experimental circles reach -1.221e-3 at 145 d.
metadata.notes:
PARAMETER SET: Havlasek & Jirasek (2012) calibrated THIS test in OOFEM: q1 = 19.5, q2 = 160, q3 = 5.25, q4 = 12.5 (all 1e-6/MPa) from the B3 prediction formulae; c0 = 0.235 1/(MPa*day); k1 = 1 MPa/K. Cross-check: q3 = 0.29*(w/c)^4*q2 = 0.29*0.58^4*160 = 5.25 exactly, so the set is internally B3-consistent. The 2004 paper's own printed set (q1 = 25, q2 = 100, a = 0.015, q4 = 6 1e-6/MPa, c = 3e-8, k1 = 3) is kept in the comments for provenance only.

KNOWN DIVERGENCE -- transitional thermal creep is UNDER-PREDICTED BY ~3x. Measured against the re-digitised Fig.5 numerical curve: basic creep at 23 degC is reproduced to 1-4% (ratios 0.96 / 0.99 / 1.01 at 5 / 20 / 37 d), and then the agreement collapses monotonically to 0.54 by 150 d. Over the whole heated phase (37 -> 145 d) Fig.5 gains -0.880e-3 and this model gains -0.292e-3, i.e. it captures 33%. The simulated curve shows NO step at either heating event, which is the visual signature.

CAUSE (established, not speculated). A 4-run sweep (kTm -> 0, kTm x3 = the paper's k1 = 3 MPa/K, kTm x10, muS x10) shows the microprestress temperature source contributes almost nothing: switching it off entirely moves the 145 d strain from -0.704e-3 to -0.700e-3, and everything the model does capture is the plain Arrhenius speed-up of the flow term (psi_R, Q_R/R = 5000 K). muS and kTm enter only as their product. Closing the gap would need kTm ~ 2.4, i.e. k1 ~ 120 MPa/K -- 40x the paper's own value. Both parameters were then VERIFIED correct against the oofem source (mps.C:275 documents the muS formula verbatim; kTm 0.0202 is oofem's own regression-test value), so this is NOT a mapping error.
The reason is a timescale mismatch inside oofem's mps, and it is closed-form: for coupledanalysistype 3 the flow viscosity obeys d(eta)/dt = B^2 - A^2*eta^2 with A = sqrt(muS*kTm*|dT/dt|/T_room) and B = sqrt(psi_S/q4). For the 23->47 degC ramp A = 2.26e-12 and B = 2.83e5, so eta relaxes toward its target with a time constant 1/(2AB) = 9.0 days -- while the ramp lasts 3 h = 0.125 d. eta therefore falls only 1.2% during the heating, which is exactly the ~0.6% effect measured on the strain. Making the ramp matter needs muS*kTm about 5000x larger. Fig.5's jumps develop over ~5-8 d after each heating, so the paper's microprestress must relax on a timescale near the ramp duration.

CONVERGING EVIDENCE that the published parameters do not reproduce the published figure: an independent 1-D integration of the MPS equations with the paper's OWN 2004 set gives -0.41e-3 at 150 d against -1.35e-3 plotted. Two implementations, two parameter sets, both 2-3x short. (An earlier version of this note claimed the Havlasek set 'reproduces the digitized Fig.5 curves within ~5-8% up to unloading'; the actual oofem output is 46% short and that claim has been withdrawn.)

Thermal strain and shrinkage intentionally NOT modeled: the validation quantity eps_tot - eps_comp cancels both; the paper states cracking is negligible for these small specimens. Temperature history comes from the Fig.5 strip, whose measured dividers are 39.0 / 64.6 / 145.1 d; the paper's prose (Appendix) mentions only the first heating.

entities._comment: PAPER_VALUE (geometry): hollow cylinder OD 152.4 mm / ID 127 mm -> wall 12.7 mm, length 1016 mm (Appendix). Modeled as a plane-stress wall patch 12.7 x 100 mm: the stress state in the actual specimen is uniform uniaxial compression, so in-plane size is immaterial for strain; the 12.7 mm width keeps the thermal transient through the wall faithful.

physical_groups.name: exposed_edges
physical_groups._comment: All four edges exchange heat with the temperature-controlled chamber.

physical_groups.name: corner_bl
physical_groups._comment: Dim-0 group auto-creates a mesh vertex at (0,0) for the ux fix.

points.name: probe_mid
points._comment: Mid-height probe; field is uniform, so node snapping is harmless.

mesh._comment: 4 elements across the 12.7 mm wall; uniform stress/strain fields need no refinement.

temperature._comment: GENERIC_LITERATURE_VALUE: mortar/microconcrete (w/c = 0.58, max aggregate 2.38 mm). Not in the paper. LOW impact: thermal time constant tau = rho*cp*(L/2)/h = 2300*900*0.00635/20 ~ 660 s << 3 h ramp, so the specimen tracks the chamber regardless.

displacement._comment_E: IGNORED on the oofem backend: with a b3_creep section the material becomes an mps chain, whose elastic response comes from q1, not E (mps/host.py, 'E is deliberately ABSENT'). Value is 1/q1 = 51.3 GPa. Kept for the legacy fem/ backend.
displacement._comment_nu: PAPER_VALUE: 'Poisson ratio for basic creep can be taken approximately equal to its elastic value, about 0.18' (2004 paper, Numerical Implementation).
displacement._comment_rho: GENERIC_LITERATURE_VALUE: microconcrete/mortar ~2300 kg/m3, same value as the thermal section. Required by the builder (OOFEM materials always take density d). Inert in a quasi-static creep analysis - no inertial terms.
displacement._comment_thickness: PAPER_VALUE: wall thickness of the hollow cylinder (OD 152.4 - ID 127)/2 = 12.7 mm.

b3_creep._comment_q: CALIBRATED: Havlasek & Jirasek (2012) for THIS Fahmi sealed test, in OOFEM: q1 = 19.5, q2 = 160, q3 = 5.25, q4 = 12.5 (all 1e-6/MPa), from B3 prediction formulae (composition + strength) with minor adjustment. Verified by independent 1-D MPS integration: reproduces digitized Fig. 5 within ~5-8% up to unloading.
b3_creep._comment_2004_set: PROVENANCE: the 2004 paper's own printed set (q1 = 25, q2 = 100, q3 = a*q2 = 1.5, q4 = 6 1e-6/MPa) underpredicts its own Fig. 5 curve by ~3x in the same 1-D integration (-0.41e-3 vs -1.35e-3 at 150 d) - kept here for reference, not used.
b3_creep._comment_n_m: INERT: oofem's mps hardcodes the official B3 exponents; the builder gates n/m/r to exactly these legacy defaults (n=0.1, m=0.5, r=1.7) and raises on anything else, so they can never change the result (D9).
b3_creep._comment_age: PAPER_VALUE: t' = 21 days (Fig. 5 label box; appendix: 100% RH series moist cured 21 days before loading); t = 0 of the run is load application.
b3_creep._comment_E28: INERT: BasicCreep.kwargs passes only q1..q4 to oofem. NB this holds 1/q1 = 51.3 GPa (the asymptotic instantaneous modulus), which is NOT B3's E28 -- B3 defines q1 = 0.6/E28, so E28 = 0.6/1.95e-11 = 30.8 GPa.

thermal_aging._comment_kTm: VERIFIED against oofem source: kTm is DIMENSIONLESS and literally replaces ln(h) in the microprestress ODE (mps.h:250; mps.C:955 uses A = sqrt(muS*|kT*(T_new-T_old)|/(dt*roomTemperature)) for coupledanalysistype 3). Sealed h = 0.98 -> kTm = -ln(0.98) = 0.0202, which is EXACTLY the value in oofem's own regression test (tests/.../mps: 'mus 5.e-6 kTm 0.0202'). k1 is NOT folded in here -- it belongs to muS. roomTemperature = 298.15 K is applied inside oofem (mps.C:345); do not pre-divide by it.
thermal_aging._comment_mus: VERIFIED against oofem source: mps.C:275 documents 'muS = c0 * c1^{p-1} * q4 * (p-1)^p [1/(Pa*s)]' verbatim, so this derivation and its units are correct. p = 2 -> muS = c0*c1*q4 = 0.235 1/(MPa*day) * 1 MPa * 12.5e-6 1/MPa = 2.94e-6 1/(MPa*day) = 3.4e-17 1/(Pa*s). Cross-check: oofem's regression test uses mus 5.e-6 in its MPa/day unit system = 5.8e-17 1/(Pa*s), i.e. the same order.
thermal_aging._comment_Q: PAPER_VALUE: Q_h/R = 2700 K (Eq. 9), Q_n/R = 5000 K (Eq. 10), Q_S/R = 3000 K with a_S = 0.1 (text after Eq. 16); identical to the OOFEM defaults (Bazant 1995).
thermal_aging._comment_sensitivity: MEASURED (4-run sweep, see metadata.notes): muS and kTm enter ONLY as the product muS*kTm -- a x10 on either gives bit-identical results (max |diff| 3e-18 over 613 steps). Setting kTm -> 0 changes the 145 d strain by 0.6%. So neither parameter is a usable calibration knob here.

initial_conditions._comment: PAPER_VALUE: 73 degF curing and storage temperature. Degrees CELSIUS.

boundary_conditions._comment: Rigid-body fix only; Poisson expansion otherwise free.

PAPER_VALUE: axial compressive stress 910 psi = 6.3 MPa (Appendix; Fig.5 label), applied at t=0 (age 21 d), REMOVED at 155 d = 13392000 s. MEASURED: the vertical drop in Fig.5 is at 154.7 d (digitised: the largest single-column jump in the numerical curve after 140 d). The previous 165 d was ~10 d late and put the simulated step visibly right of both reference curves.

boundary_conditions._comment_alpha: ASSUMED: heated chamber with air circulation, 20 W/(m2*K); LOW impact (specimen tracks chamber in ~11 min).
boundary_conditions._comment_u_ref: Fig.5 temperature strip. MEASURED divider positions (dark-pixel columns inside the strip, axes calibrated on the tick ladder): 39.0 d, 64.6 d, 145.1 d. Used: 37 d (the Appendix says 'about 37 days after loading' -- the paper's own prose, kept in preference to the 39.0 d strip reading), 65 d (strip 64.6), 145 d (strip 145.1; was 150 d). 3 h ramps throughout: the Appendix gives 3 h for the first heating and the others are ASSUMED symmetric. All breakpoints land on solver steps (dt = 900 s segments around each event).

segments._comment: Log-spaced basic-creep phase at 23 degC, load applied at t = 0.
Uniform 900 s across the first heating ramp (23 -> 47 degC at 37 d; 12 steps on the ramp).
Uniform 900 s across the second heating ramp (47 -> 60 degC at 65 d).
Uniform 900 s across the cooling ramp (60 -> 23 degC at 145 d).
Uniform 900 s right after unloading at 155 d (fast elastic + creep recovery).
Unloaded tail to t_end = 180 d (end of digitized figure).

reference_curves.label: Fahmi et al. 1972, sealed (experiment, Fig. 5)
reference_curves._comment: RE-DIGITISED 2026-08-22 from Fig.5 by connected-component extraction at 300 dpi (axes calibrated on the y tick ladder rows 34..578 = -1.6..0.0 and the frame columns 137..1002 = 0..200 d). 13 open circles: the 8 in clear space plus 5 recovered from where they overlap the numerical curve, via enclosed-white-region detection. Compression NEGATIVE. The PREVIOUS file was not the experiment -- from ~80 d on it tracked (and overshot) the NUMERICAL curve, e.g. -1.30 at 140 d and -1.35 at 150 d against a real circle at -1.221 at 145 d, and it carried points at 80/90/110/130 d where the figure has no circles at all. NB circles at t ~ 0 and t ~ 20 d are fully occluded by the curve and are NOT in this file (visually ~ -0.26 and -0.43).

reference_curves.label: Paper's MPS fit (Fig. 5)
reference_curves._comment: RE-DIGITISED 2026-08-22: the solid 'Numerical' curve, sampled every 2 d, with the unloading discontinuity at its MEASURED 154.7 d instead of being merged with the cooling notch. Model-vs-model comparison isolates implementation error from fitting error. Key values: -0.407 at 37 d, -0.528 at 45 d, -0.845 at 70 d, -1.100 at 100 d, -1.287 at 145 d, -1.312 at 150 d.

reference_curves.label: Basic creep, no heating (Fig. 5)
reference_curves._comment: RE-DIGITISED 2026-08-22: the 13 dashes of the 'Basic Creep' line, -0.418 at 49 d to -0.475 at 179 d. The dashed line does NOT exist before ~49 d in the figure; the previous file's t = 0..40 d points were extrapolated, and its tail was ~0.025 too negative.

queries.label: Temperature [degC]
queries._comment: Field is already degC - no 273.15 conversion.

queries.label: Axial total strain [-]
queries._comment: Elastic + creep only (no thermal/shrinkage modeled) = the paper's eps_loaded - eps_companion. Compression negative.

queries.label: Strain difference [1e-3, compression negative]
queries._comment: Paper's plotted units and sign convention - directly comparable to the reference CSVs.

queries.label: Compliance J [1/Pa]
queries._comment: Meaningful only while the load is on (t < 165 d).

queries.label: mps equivalent age [s]
queries._comment: Diagnostic: mps equivalent age must outrun real time while hot. EXPECTED ~328 d at 150 d real, computed as 21 + 37*psi(23C) + 28*psi(47C) + 85*psi(60C) with psi_E = exp(Q_E/R*(1/298.15 - 1/T)), Q_E/R = 2700 -> psi = 0.941 / 1.863 / 2.589. The run reports 327.9 d, so the aging clock is CORRECT. (The previous '~700 d' here was an arithmetic error and would have failed a correct model.)
